cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: swallow all test/build/lint output and replace it with a single ✓ if the stage passes
cards.claim: Wrap test/build/lint commands so passing stages print one tick and only failing stages dump their full captured output.
cards.evidence_detail: Used constantly at HumanLayer; a run_silent shell function is given; no numbers beyond a 'half a context window' estimate for their monorepo checks.
cards.landing: A run_silent wrapper script used by the phase routine's check commands (backend ruff/mypy/pytest, web lint/test, mobile typecheck/jest); named in CLAUDE.md Commands.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: stay in the ~75k token "smart zone" for claude models
cards.claim: Keep the working context under roughly 75k tokens (the smart zone) and treat every passing-test line as wasted context.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as a target number; no experiment given. Says a passing run wastes 2-3% of the window for under 10 tokens of information.
cards.landing: A context budget rule in the phase routine (one phase per new session) with a ~75k reference figure; relates to compaction trigger.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: human time wasted on wrangling an agent in the dumb zone is likely more expensive by 10x
cards.claim: Token cost and run time of checks are secondary; human time lost to an agent in the dumb zone costs 10x or more.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as likely; no data.
cards.landing: Cost-model argument for effort routing and context discipline: optimise human time and context, not tokens.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Rather than letting the model decide what to truncate, we like to take control of output deterministically.
cards.claim: Decide truncation in a deterministic wrapper (success = tick, failure = full output) rather than leaving it to the model.
cards.evidence_detail: Design principle, illustrated with an example output.
cards.landing: Output caps in the harness are currently the model's choice or fixed caps; replace with exit-code-gated wrappers in scripts the routine calls.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Enable failFast. pytest -x , jest --bail , go test -failfast . One failure at a time.
cards.claim: Run test suites fail-fast so the agent sees one failure at a time instead of context-switching between several.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation, no numbers.
cards.landing: Check commands for backend (pytest -x) and web/mobile (jest --bail) in the routine's inner loop; full run only before PR.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Strip generic stack frames that don't help your agent find the issue. Remove timing info.
cards.claim: Filter failure output (stack frames, timings, framework parsing for counts) down to the assertion that failed.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation; mentions a hacky run_silent.sh extracting counts from pytest, jest, go test, vitest.
cards.landing: Failure-output filters for pytest/Vitest/Jest/ruff/mypy output in a shared script.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we run these in a pre-push hook, and some subset of these projects for each plan phase.
cards.claim: The same silent check wrappers run in a pre-push hook and as a per-plan-phase subset, giving a deterministic gate.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes their own monorepo checks; would be half a context window without wrappers.
cards.landing: Re-opens the skipped pre-commit/pre-push gate: a hook that runs the wrappers is also a non-self-reported compliance signal (mark: re-opens skipped hooks/pre-commit gate).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Now your only job is to convince the model not to do its own truncation.
cards.claim: After installing wrappers, the remaining work is instructing the model not to pipe output through head/tail or /dev/null itself.
cards.evidence_detail: Suggests shouting in claude.md; no measure.
cards.landing: One short universal line in CLAUDE.md Commands ('run checks via the wrapper; never pipe to head/tail').

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it ran a 5 minute test suite with head -n 50 and now it has to run it again
cards.claim: Context-anxious models pipe output to head/tail or /dev/null, then rerun slow suites, burning more tokens and human time than they save.
cards.evidence_detail: Reported complaints and a pytest | head -n 50 example; a trivial case where /dev/null guards cost more tokens (unofficial tokenizer).
cards.landing: A known model failure mode to forbid in the routine for slow suites (backend integration tests against Postgres).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: deterministic is better than non-deterministic. If you already know what matters, don't leave it to a model
cards.claim: If you already know what matters in an output, a deterministic filter beats having the model churn through junk tokens.
cards.evidence_detail: Closing principle.
cards.landing: General design rule for the harness: prefer scripts over instructions where the check is knowable.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: every token you use is diminishing the results and moves you closer to "need to clear or compact
cards.claim: Each token of context diminishes result quality and moves the session toward a forced clear or compaction.
cards.evidence_detail: Assertion tied to the smart/dumb zone idea.
cards.landing: Supports the one-phase-per-session defence; candidate rationale line in the phase routine.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: labs have to take big swings and the majority of their potential user base doesn't know how
cards.claim: Recent models are RL-trained to be conservative about loading context, which compensates for context-inefficient codebases but hurts careful users.
cards.evidence_detail: Speculation, explicitly flagged as opining.
cards.landing: Explains why wrappers must be paired with an explicit no-truncation instruction; model-behaviour caveat for harness prompts.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Frontier thinking LLMs can follow ~ 150-200 instructions with reasonable consistency.
cards.claim: Frontier thinking models follow about 150-200 instructions consistently; smaller and non-thinking models fewer, and smaller models decay exponentially.
cards.evidence_detail: Cites unspecified research 'not investigated in an incredibly rigorous manner'; no numbers on decay beyond the claim.
cards.landing: Instruction budget for CLAUDE.md trim: count instructions, not lines (390 lines is well above).

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Claude Code's system prompt contains ~50 individual instructions
cards.claim: The Claude Code system prompt already uses about 50 instructions, nearly a third of the reliable budget, before CLAUDE.md, skills or user messages.
cards.evidence_detail: Claimed from their analysis of the harness (logging proxy); no breakdown given.
cards.landing: Budget arithmetic for CLAUDE.md plus skills: each new skill/agent description eats the same instruction budget.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: As instruction count increases, instruction-following quality decreases uniformly.
cards.claim: More instructions do not make the model ignore only the later ones; it ignores all of them uniformly, with bias toward the start and end of the prompt.
cards.evidence_detail: Attributed to loose research; no source given.
cards.landing: Argues against appending invariants to the bottom of CLAUDE.md; put the few critical ones first and last, move the rest out.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: IMPORTANT: this context may or may not be relevant to your tasks.
cards.claim: Claude Code wraps CLAUDE.md in a system reminder telling the model to ignore it unless highly relevant, so non-universal content gets ignored.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed via a logging proxy on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; rationale for Anthropic's choice is speculation.
cards.landing: Every non-universal line in CLAUDE.md lowers compliance with the rest; basis for moving phase-specific rules into skills. The proxy method is also a way to observe what the agent actually saw (marks: measurement pipeline skipped).

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: general consensus is that < 300 lines is best, and shorter is even better.
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md should stay under 300 lines; HumanLayer's own root file is under sixty.
cards.evidence_detail: Consensus claim plus their own file length.
cards.landing: Target for the CLAUDE.md trim (390 lines now; <300 ceiling, ~60 as their example).

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: keeping task-specific instructions in separate markdown files with self-descriptive names
cards.claim: Use progressive disclosure: an agent_docs/ folder of task-specific files, listed in CLAUDE.md with one-line descriptions for the agent to choose from.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation with example file layout; compared to how Skills work.
cards.landing: Move the invariant sections (outbox, bill freeze, dispatcher) to per-area docs or skills with descriptions; CLAUDE.md keeps an index.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Prefer pointers to copies . Don't include code snippets in these files if possible
cards.claim: Reference file:line pointers to authoritative code rather than copying snippets, which go stale.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation.
cards.landing: Audit CLAUDE.md for stated facts (Alembic head, table counts) that duplicate code and rot; replace with pointers or a check script.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Never send an LLM to do a linter's job .
cards.claim: Do not put code style rules in CLAUDE.md; use deterministic linters/formatters (ideally auto-fixing) and let in-context learning follow existing patterns.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation; mentions Biome.
cards.landing: Prune style rules from CLAUDE.md; rely on ruff/prettier/eslint already in CI.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: consider setting up a Claude Code Stop hook that runs your formatter & linter
cards.claim: A Stop hook that runs formatter and linter and feeds errors back to the agent replaces asking the agent to find formatting issues.
cards.evidence_detail: Suggestion for those who feel strongly; slash command alternative separates implementation from formatting.
cards.landing: Re-opens the skipped hooks decision: a Stop hook is both backpressure and an observable compliance record (mark: re-opens hooks).

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: A bad line of a research that misunderstands how the system works has the potential to result in a lot of bad lines
cards.claim: Errors compound down the pipeline (bad research line, bad plan lines, bad code), and CLAUDE.md touches every phase, so every line deserves scrutiny.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument; no data.
cards.landing: Justifies review leverage at research/plan artefacts and a line-by-line CLAUDE.md audit.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: we think you should spend some time thinking very carefully about every single line
cards.claim: Do not auto-generate CLAUDE.md with /init; hand-craft it because it is the highest-leverage point of the harness.
cards.evidence_detail: Recommendation.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md is hand-written already; guard against agent-appended additions in phase PRs (changes to CLAUDE.md need review).

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Smaller models get MUCH worse, MUCH more quickly .
cards.claim: Smaller models decay exponentially in instruction following, so avoid small models for multi-step tasks or complicated plans.
cards.evidence_detail: Cited research, not named.
cards.landing: Caution on the Haiku locator agent: keep its instruction set tiny and single-purpose; do not give small models multi-step plans.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: CLAUDE.md onboards Claude to your codebase
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md should cover WHAT (stack, map), WHY (purpose), HOW (build, test, verify) and not every possible command.
cards.evidence_detail: Framework recommendation.
cards.landing: Structure template for the trimmed CLAUDE.md: map, purpose, verification commands, index of deeper docs.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you'll ALWAYS get better results with a small, focused prompt and context
cards.claim: Even as context windows grow, a small focused context beats a long one; loops past 10-20 turns become unrecoverable messes.
cards.evidence_detail: Based on conversations with builders; no experiment.
cards.landing: Rationale for one phase per new session; a turn-count ceiling per phase in the routine.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: keeping agents focused on specific domains with 3-10, maybe 20 steps max
cards.claim: Keep agents to small scopes of 3-10 (max ~20) steps so context stays manageable.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule of thumb.
cards.landing: Sizing guide for custom agents and workflow steps (the Haiku locator, future skills) and for phase size.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Agents, at least the good ones, are comprised of mostly just software.
cards.claim: Good agent systems are mostly deterministic code with LLM steps at chosen points; own control flow rather than looping until done.
cards.evidence_detail: Observations from founders and his own deploy bot; no numbers.
cards.landing: Supports saving workflows as scripts (deterministic control flow, LLM steps in slots) instead of ad hoc prompts; hooks/scripts over instructions.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Consider hiding errors and failed calls from context window once they are resolved.
cards.claim: Prune resolved errors from context, restructure how errors are represented, and cap consecutive errors (~3) before escalating to a human.
cards.evidence_detail: Code example with errorCounter; no data.
cards.landing: Rule for refuter/verifier loops: a retry cap (3) then escalate to owner; do not keep failed attempts in the next verifier's context.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we need to be able to interrupt a working agent and resume later
cards.claim: Agents must be pausable between tool selection and tool execution so humans can approve high-stakes calls; without it you restrict to low-risk work or yolo.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as his number one framework feature request; deploybot example.
cards.landing: Approval-gate shape for irreversible steps (railway up, migrations); a hook-based pre-tool approval is the Claude Code analogue (re-opens hooks).
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can engineer your application so that you can infer all execution state from the context window
cards.claim: Unify execution state and business state in one serialisable thread so you can resume, fork, debug, and render it for humans.
cards.evidence_detail: Benefits list: simplicity, serialisation, recovery, forking, observability.
cards.landing: Cold-resume principle: a phase's state should be recoverable from the repo artefacts (journal, PR body) alone, which is what P1's trial tests.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Everything is context engineering. LLMs are stateless functions that turn inputs into outputs.
cards.claim: Output quality depends only on the inputs assembled per call: prompt, retrieved docs, history, memory, output instructions.
cards.evidence_detail: Core thesis of Factor 3.
cards.landing: Framing for the knowledge-store: what a fresh agent knows is only what the store/repo puts in its context.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Own your prompts and treat them as first-class code
cards.claim: Prompts should be owned, versioned and tested with evals like code rather than outsourced to a framework.
cards.evidence_detail: Benefits list: control, testing, iteration, transparency.
cards.landing: Treat skill/agent prompt files and the phase routine as code: versioned, with a test (the cold-resume trial is such a test).
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Even as models support longer and longer context windows
cards.claim: Micro agents inside a deterministic DAG make it easy to take human feedback into workflow steps without context error loops; keep scope small now and widen only as reliability allows.
cards.evidence_detail: Real deploy agent example (HumanLayer's own); no numbers.
cards.landing: Design rule for workflow library: deterministic outer script, small agent steps; widen scope only after measured reliability.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Own Your Control Flow
cards.claim: Own control flow to add summarisation of tool results, LLM-as-judge on structured output, compaction, tracing, rate limiting, and durable waits.
cards.evidence_detail: List of control-flow hooks in Factor 8 with code.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts as the owned control flow: judge panels, tracing of which steps ran (answers 'routine skipped?' from the script log).
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do not outsource the thinking
cards.claim: Six-phase QRSPI (Questions, Research, Design, Structure, Plan, Implement) puts a human checkpoint at every phase so the agent shows what it is wrong about before implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Product copy; no data. Phases described in one line each.
cards.landing: Compare to the 40-phase routine's structure; a questions-first step and a design-doc review before the plan.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Catch mistakes before 2,000 lines of code.
cards.claim: Review comments on a design doc, with decisions feeding back to the agent, catch errors earlier than reviewing code.
cards.evidence_detail: Copy; mockup of a design review shown.
cards.landing: Owner review at design/plan artefact (PR 'Plan @ sha' body) rather than only at the end; keep decisions journal as the feedback channel.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: What we are not doing
cards.claim: The design doc template includes Current State, Desired End State and an explicit 'what we are not doing' list.
cards.evidence_detail: Seen in the mockup design doc only.
cards.landing: Plan template section for the PR body: explicit out-of-scope list per phase.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Compounding Engineering — Agents get smarter over time
cards.claim: Pro tier advertises compounding engineering (agents improve with use) and a 'workflow preview' of staged sessions with a per-task artifact set (research.md, design.md, structure.md, plan.md).
cards.evidence_detail: Feature bullet only.
cards.landing: Per-task artifact folder convention (research, design, plan) and reviewed memory feeding future runs; relates to the knowledge-store design.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: making the prompts and workflows "squishy" - that is, flexible to a broad range of problems
cards.claim: Opinionated workflows are tuned to be flexible to varied inputs so there is no holding it wrong, after hundreds of hours with customers.
cards.evidence_detail: FAQ copy; no data.
cards.landing: Workflow library design: parameterised, tolerant of different task shapes rather than one script per task.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: You can’t do advanced context engineering without staying in touch with your context.
cards.claim: Full visibility into every thinking message and subagent call is needed to do context engineering.
cards.evidence_detail: Copy.
cards.landing: Observability of sessions (transcripts/evidence folders) as the basis for knowing whether the routine was followed; re-opens the measurement pipeline skipped item.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Execute with continuous feedback. No 2,000-line surprises.
cards.claim: Implementation runs against a phased, verifiable structure outline with file paths, test cases and acceptance criteria written first.
cards.evidence_detail: Phase descriptions Structure and Plan.
cards.landing: Plan must name file paths, tests and acceptance criteria per phase; fits the 'fail-before/pass-after per register id' reviewer demand.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: one-shot tests, token use, and task count do not measure whether code stays easy to change
cards.claim: Software factories fail because one-shot tests, token use and task count do not measure maintainability; the harness is only one part of a factory.
cards.evidence_detail: Index blurb summarising the July 2026 essay; the essay itself is not read here.
cards.landing: Do not use test pass or task count as the harness's success signal; need maintainability checks in verifiers.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: read the code, seek leverage, and break skills into workflows
cards.claim: After five months of a lights-off factory drowned them in slop, revised advice is read the code, seek leverage, and split skills into workflows.
cards.evidence_detail: Index summary of their own experience; no numbers here.
cards.landing: Argues for splitting big skills into explicit multi-step workflows (saved library), and keeping human reading of code in the loop.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: RPI became a way to outsource thought, and how QRSPI turns it into explicit control flow
cards.claim: RPI as giant prompts let people outsource thought; QRSPI replaces them with smaller workflows with explicit control flow and more human ownership.
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb for the Apr 2026 talk after rolling RPI out to hundreds of engineers.
cards.landing: Risk flag for the phase routine as one long prompt: break into steps with control flow in a workflow script.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If teams replace code review with loops and stop reading code, one failure can leave nobody able to recover.
cards.claim: The software factory existential risk: if nobody reads the code, a single failure leaves nobody able to recover.
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb for X posts, 1.1M combined views, Mar 2026.
cards.landing: Keep owner reading of key diffs/artefacts in the routine; do not remove human review for automated reviewer alone.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why review agents do not solve the slop problem
cards.claim: Review agents do not fix slop (listed as an idea title in the Feb-May 2026 era).
cards.evidence_detail: Title only on this page; argument is in an X thread not read here.
cards.landing: Challenges the Opus reviewer per PR and refuter-first design as sufficient; needs earlier-stage (design/plan) review.
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 threads (Why review agents do not solve slop)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Bash considered harmful
cards.claim: A listed idea in the Feb-May 2026 era: bash as a general tool is harmful to agents (content not given on this page).
cards.evidence_detail: Title only.
cards.landing: Possible tool-permission restriction for sub-agents; unknown content, flag for another reader.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Learning tests and proof-driven development
cards.claim: Learning tests and proof-driven development are listed as ideas; Backpressure Deep Dive blurb says learning tests help agents test assumptions and recover from bad paths.
cards.evidence_detail: Title and one blurb sentence.
cards.landing: Learning test for each external assumption in a phase plan (e.g. Railway, pooler behaviour) written before implementation.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Problems with default compaction
cards.claim: Default compaction is listed as having problems; the earlier era's method is frequent intentional compaction instead.
cards.evidence_detail: Title and era summary only.
cards.landing: Do not rely on auto-compact; handoff documents at phase end (already one phase per session).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why larger windows weaken instruction use, and why small, isolated contexts work better
cards.claim: Larger context windows weaken instruction use; small isolated contexts work better for hard coding tasks (the Long-Context post, by Kyle).
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb only; the post is by Kyle and reports switching back from 1M context.
cards.landing: Keep sessions on the standard window and isolate verifier contexts; supports one phase per session over 1M-token sessions.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a little planning removes most expected rework, while polishing every detail up front wastes time
cards.claim: Pragmatic leverage: a little up-front planning removes most expected rework, but over-polishing every detail wastes time.
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb for a July 2026 X article.
cards.landing: Plan depth calibration per phase: light plan for mechanical phases, heavier for risky ones.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: product review, system design, program design, and vertical slices cut rework before code review
cards.claim: Product review, system design, program design and vertical slices cut rework before code review.
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb for X article part 2.
cards.landing: Slice-shaped phases (the repo already uses vertical slices); program-design step before phases start.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Opus 5 passed 4 of 17 checkpoints while every model added defects and more complex code
cards.claim: SlopCodeBench reports: Opus 5 passed 4 of 17 checkpoints; Fable and Sol tied at 33.3% on a larger run; all models accumulated defects across checkpoints.
cards.evidence_detail: Benchmark blurbs: 4/17, 33.3% tie, 24% strict pass rate (HN blurb).
cards.landing: Models degrade code quality over repeated changes; justify maintainability-focused verifiers over test-pass.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: A skill that asks agents to explain code, plans, and diffs with compact diagrams instead of long prose.
cards.claim: A /show-me skill makes agents explain code, plans and diffs with compact diagrams, trees and diffs instead of prose.
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb; 798k views for the X article.
cards.landing: A show-me style skill for the owner one-page view and reviewer summaries.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Agents as code rotators
cards.claim: Listed idea title: agents as code rotators (content not given here).
cards.evidence_detail: Title only.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious; flag for another reader.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Designing AI systems for human leverage and why models cannot architect
cards.claim: Listed idea title: models cannot architect, so AI systems should be designed for human leverage (content not given here).
cards.evidence_detail: Title only.
cards.landing: Architecture decisions stay with owner/design phase; flag for another reader.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Context forking
cards.claim: Context forking (build high-quality context once, reuse it multiple times) is a listed idea and a May 2026 Kyle post.
cards.evidence_detail: Title on this page; blog index blurb describes it as a primitive for reusing built-up context.
cards.landing: Fork a researched session into parallel verifiers/implementers instead of re-reading; fits fresh-context refuters with a shared base.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Using conditional XML blocks to make Claude pay attention to the right instructions at the right time.
cards.claim: Wrap task-specific CLAUDE.md sections in conditional XML blocks so Claude attends to them only when relevant (March 2026 post).
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb only; the post is not in this bundle.
cards.landing: Cheap partial answer to the CLAUDE.md trim: conditional blocks for the invariant sections.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why "spec is the new code" is not enough
cards.claim: Specs alone are not enough as the new code; RPI versus spec-driven development is a recurring argument.
cards.evidence_detail: Titles only; 'No Vibes Allowed' blurb says spec-driven dev is the wrong way to think.
cards.landing: Do not treat the ship plan as the code; implementation needs research and reading of the code per phase.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the weaker plan produced when the agent skipped codebase research
cards.claim: A live test showed the plan was weaker when the agent skipped codebase research (AI That Works #17).
cards.evidence_detail: Blurb for a single live session.
cards.landing: Research step must be evidenced before plan; a reviewer check that the research artefact exists.

cards.source_title: How three YC startups built their companies with Claude Code
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Don't make Claude do research while it's trying to plan, while it's trying to implement
cards.claim: Separate research, plan and implement into discrete sessions, passing only distilled conclusions forward; Ambral's CTO says this was influenced by Horthy's work.
cards.evidence_detail: Quote from Ambral CTO Stettner; Anthropic editorial; no numbers.
cards.landing: Confirms one phase per new session; handoff must carry only distilled conclusions.

cards.source_title: How three YC startups built their companies with Claude Code
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Opus 4.1 to do research and planning. Sonnet 4.5 has been absolutely killer
cards.claim: Use the stronger model for research and planning and a cheaper model to implement each plan phase.
cards.evidence_detail: One CTO's practice; not Dex's own claim.
cards.landing: Model routing per phase type; compare to the xhigh-everywhere verifier setup.

cards.source_title: How three YC startups built their companies with Claude Code
cards.author: other
cards.quote: it's generally due to a contradiction that I have in a prompt somewhere
cards.claim: Unexpected low-quality output usually traces to a contradiction in the prompt; be deliberate about what enters context and when to start new conversations.
cards.evidence_detail: Stettner's experience.
cards.landing: Audit CLAUDE.md, skills and ship-plan prose for contradicting rules (e.g. doc drift vs CLAUDE.md).

cards.source_title: How three YC startups built their companies with Claude Code
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: after we spent 7 hours shipping what would normally be 1-2 weeks of work
cards.claim: A 7-hour pairing session with Vaibhav shipped what would normally take 1-2 weeks, which convinced Horthy the workflow generalises.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's account, relayed by Anthropic; single session, unmeasured baseline.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (motivation, not a mechanism).

cards.source_title: How three YC startups built their companies with Claude Code
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you have a completely different type of problem... a communication, collaboration, tooling, and management problem
cards.claim: Once several people ship AI-written code, the bottleneck is team communication, collaboration, tooling and management, not individual use.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex quote; Q4 2025 pilots claimed.
cards.landing: Shared artefacts and a saved workflow library so the routine does not depend on one operator's chat habits.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Have your finger on the trigger to escape and interrupt any bad behavior.
cards.claim: Watch the chain of thought and interrupt within the first few tool calls, since catching a wrong direction early saves more than letting a misguided run finish.
cards.evidence_detail: Vulcan CEO advice; not Dex.
cards.landing: An early checkpoint (first N tool calls) where the phase plan is confirmed before long runs; nowhere obvious in unattended workflows.
